The petitioner has filed the present claim petition under section 166 & 140 of M.V. Act claiming compensation of Rs.5,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 27.03.2012.
MAC NO.209/12 SANJAY V/S. JAI SINGH & ORS. 1/13 2.

The facts as setup by the petitioner in his petition are that on 27.03.2012 at about 9.15 pm while he was going on his Motorcycle, he was hit by a Car make Ambassador bearing registration no. DL 1CJ5552 (hereinafter referred as offending vehicle), from behind, which was driven by its driver at a high speed and rash manner.
He fell down and sustained injuries and was taken to LBS Hospital.

A case was registered against the Respondent no. 1 vide FIR no. 89/12, PS Pandav Nagar u/s.
279/338 IPC .
3. It is stated by the Petitioner that the Respondent no.1 is the Driver and Respondent no.2 is the Sh. Sanjay S/O.

sentences.text: The Respondent no. 1 in his Written Statement has stated that the petitioner himself was negligent while driving his motorcycle in a zig zag manner without caring for safety rules; that the injured was taken to LBS Hospital by Responent no. 1 in the offending vehicle.

1.Whether
Petitioner suffered injuries in road side accident on 27.03.2012 involving vehicle i.e. Car bearing registration no. DL1CJ5552 being driven allegedly in a rash and negligent manner by R 1?

2. To what amount of compensation, if any, the MAC NO.209/12 SANJAY V/S. JAI SINGH & ORS.

sentences.text: Petitioner examined himself as PW1 and filed his affidavit as Ex. PW1/A.

He proved the documents i.e., DAR as Ex. PW1/1, Medical Bills as Ex. PW1/2, Treatment Record as Ex. PW1/3, his Driving License as Ex. PW1/4, Disability Certificate as Ex. PW1/5 Salary Slips as Ex.

from GTB Hospital, proved the Disability Certificate as Ex.PW1/5 mentioning 29% permanent disability in relation to right upper & right lower limb suffered by the Petitioner.
7. It is pertinent to mention that Respondents have not brought any evidence in support of their contentions.
8. This court has carefully heard Ld. Counsels for parties in the light of relevant statutory provisions of law.

On the basis of submissions advanced and the evidence adduced, my observations on the issues are as follows : ISSUE NO.1 :
Whether Petitioner has suffered injuries in road side accident on 27.03.2012 involving vehicle i.e. Car bearing registration no. DL1CJ5552 being driven allegedly in a rash and negligent manner by R1?
9.

For succeeding in a Petition filed under the provisions of 166 and 140 of the M.V. Act, it is for the Petitioner to prove that the vehicle which caused the accident was being driven rashly and MAC NO.209/12 SANJAY V/S. JAI SINGH & ORS. 3/13 negligently by its driver.
PW1 testified that on 27.03.2012 at about 9.15 pm, he was going on his Motorcycle when he was hit by a Car make Ambassador bearing registration no. DL1CJ5552 from behind.
He testified that the offending vehicle was driven in rash and negligent manner and rammed into his motorcycle.
He testified that on account of accident, he sustained serious injuries and the resultant permanent disability.

sentences.text: Counsel for the respondents argued that the entire petition does not specify the exact manner of the accident.
It is argued that Petitioner stated to have been hit by the offending vehicle coming from behind, but the Mechanical Inspection Reports of both vehicles points out contrary to this.
It is argued that from the damages sustained by vehicles, it is clear that it was a headon collision in which the Motorcyclist himself rammed against the car.
It is argued that the accident happened due to the negligence of motorcyclist himself.
It is argued that the driver of the offending car had taken the injured to the Hospital.

Ld. Counsel has further pointed out certain discrepancies in the petition,
the affidavits as well as the final computation given by the Petitioner in respect of the variance of the amount of compensation sought besides discrepancies in the contents of the Affidavit earlier filed by the Petitioner dated 13.10.2013 and the subsequent Affidavit dated 21.05.2014.

Ld. Counsel thus,
requests for the deduction of the amount on the basis of the negligence of Petitioner, which contributed to the accident.

Ld. Counsel for the Petitioner, MAC NO.209/12 SANJAY V/S. JAI SINGH & ORS. 4/13 however, argued that the contributory negligence cannot be assumed in the absence of any supporting material having brought by the Respondents.

sentences.text: 11.I have heard Ld. Counsel for Parties.
It is worthwhile to state that no evidence has been adduced by the Respondent no. 1 & 2 i.e., Driver & Owner despite opportunity.

I hold that since the contribution of the petitioner in causing the accident is not proved by the Respondents by producing evidence, the Defence of contributory negligence has no substance as the contributory negligence is not to be assumed but has to be proved with cogent evidence.
Reliance can be placed on the judgement of Hon'ble Apex Court in Syed Sadiq etc. V/s.
United India Insurance Co. I (2014) ACC 206 SC.

sentences.text: This Court has considered the criminal proceedings including the FIR and accompanying documents.

Police after investigation has filed Chargesheet against Respondent no.1 under Sections 279/338 IPC in case FIR No.89/12, Police Station Pandav Nagar which is primafacie suggestive of negligence of Respondent no.1 in driving the vehicle at the time of accident.

I am placing reliance upon the judgments of Hon'ble Apex Court in Parmeshwari v. Amir Chand (2011) 11 SCC 635 and Kusum Lata v. Satbir, (2011) 3 SCC 646.
12.In case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Kamlesh, 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310,
an adverse inference was drawn because the driver of the offending vehicle had not appeared MAC NO.209/12 SANJAY V/S. JAI SINGH & ORS. 5/13 in the witness box to corroborate his defence taken in the written statement.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was noted that there was nothing on record to show that the Petitioner had any enmity with the driver of the offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in the case.
13.The issue thus stands decided in favour of Petitioner holding that the accident happened as a result of negligent driving by Respondent no.1, in which Petitioner received grievous injuries.

ISSUE NO.2 :
To what amount of compensation, if any, the Petitioner is entitled to and from whom?

15.Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) enjoins payment of just compensation.

In General Manager, Kerala State Road Trans. Corpn. V/s. Susamma Thomas 1994 ACJ 1 (SC), the Apex Court held as under :
"(5)........ The determination of the quantum must answer what contemporary society 'would deem MAC NO.209/12 SANJAY V/S. JAI SINGH & ORS. 6/13 to be a fair sum such as would allow the wrongdoer to hold up his head among his neighbours and say with their approval that he has done the fair thing.

sentences.text: The amount awarded must not be niggardly since the law value life and limb in a free society in generous scales'
All this means that the sum awarded must be fair and reasonable by accepted legal standards.".

16.In Nizam Institute of medical Sciences V/s. Prasanth S. Dhananka, 2010 ACJ 38 (SC), the Hon'ble Supreme Court emphasized that cases of serious injuries in the motor vehicle accident are worse than the death cases because the victim and his family suffer throughout life.

sentences.text: 17.Hon'ble Supreme Court has enumerated the principles for granting compensation payable to road traffic accident victims.

In the case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr., MANU/SC/1018/2010, Civil Appeal No. 8981/2010 decided on 18.10.2010, following principles were laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court for determining compensation payable to road traffic accident victims :
i) The compensation payable to the Petitioner who is a victim of road accident should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the Petitioner to the position prior to the accident.

entities.text: Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr., MANU/SC/1018/2010,
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equatable manner.
ii) Compensation payable in injury cases is payable under two heads.
They are pecuniary damages (special damages) and non pecuniary damages.

Pecuniary damages have three MAC NO.209/12 SANJAY V/S. JAI SINGH & ORS. 7/13 sub heads which are : (i) expenses relating to treatment,
hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) (a)
Loss of earning (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured,
comprising of loss of earning during the period of treatment and (b) loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability (iii) Future medical expenses. Nonpecuniary damages (General Damage) are (iv) damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of injuries (v) loss of amenities and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and (vi) loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).

In routine personal injury cases compensation is awarded only under heads (i), (ii) (a) and (iv).

It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the Petitioner, that compensation is granted under any of the heads (ii) (b), (iii) and (vi)
relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospectus of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
18.Petitioner is entitled for the compensation on account of the loss due to accidental injuries.
While assessing future loss, his functional disability has to be assessed, which is to be judged with reference to the nature of work being performed by him.
The Petitioner in his affidavit stated that he was working as a Driver with M/s. Green Tourist Services Pvt. Ltd. at R.K. Puram and was earning Rs. 10,000/ per month.

sentences.text: The Petitioner, however, has not produced any evidence in support of his employment or earnings.

After examining him, I assess that on account of the resultant disability,
Petitioner's general physical capacity has been reduced, restricting him from carrying out his normal work.

From overall MAC NO.209/12 SANJAY V/S. JAI SINGH & ORS. 8/13 circumstances, the functional disability of the Petitioner is taken as 10%, in relation to the whole body, in view of the dictum of "Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343".

Lalta Devi & Ors., (Decided on 12.1.2015), it was observed that the three Judge Bench Decision in Reshma Kumari & Ors. Vs. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65 was held to be taken as a binding precedent.

The Petitioner is awarded a compensation of an amount of Rs.1,43,770/ (Rs.6,656.00 x 12 x 18 x 0.10) under the head Future Loss of Income.

20.While fixing compensation for pain and sufferings, as also for loss of amenities of life, the features like the age, marital status and unusual deprivation undertaken by a person in his life are to be reckoned.

The Petitioner, however, has not filed anything in support thereof and thus, from the overall assessment of the circumstances, I assess an amount of Rs. Rs.50,000/ as compensation towards Pain, Shock and Suffering to the MAC NO.209/12 SANJAY V/S. JAI SINGH & ORS. 9/13 Petitioner.
21.From the documents, the age of the Petitioner is taken as 25 years.
Petitioner has suffered loss of expectation of life i.e., his normal life span has been affected due to the injuries.
Keeping in mind this fact, he is awarded compensation of Rs.50,000/ towards Loss of Amenities and Enjoyment of Life.
22.The
Petitioner stated in his affidavit that he remained under treatment and several operations were conducted upon him.
He stated that he incurred an amount of Rs. 2,00,000/ on his Treatment.
However, there is no supporting document to this nor any expert evidence is produced or any Doctor was examined to prove this.

26.A victim of an accident has to be compensated in terms of money even if gratuitous services are rendered by a family member.
In Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. Vs. Lalita, AIR 1981 Delhi 558, Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has held that there cannot be any deduction if domestic help is obtained from a family member.

While assessing future loss, his functional disability has to be assessed, which is to be judged with reference to the nature of work being performed by him.
From overall MAC NO.209/12 SANJAY V/S. JAI SINGH & ORS. 8/13 circumstances, the functional disability of the Petitioner is taken as 10%, in relation to the whole body, in view of the dictum of "Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343".
19.As
So far future prospects concern, in a recent judgment in HDFC Ergo General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs.
Lalta Devi & Ors., (Decided on 12.1.2015), it was observed that the three Judge Bench Decision in Reshma Kumari & Ors. Vs. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65 was held to be taken as a binding precedent.
However,
with the kind of injuries suffered by him, it can be safely assumed that he would have suffered loss of earning capacity at least for a period of four months.
In Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. Vs. Lalita, AIR 1981 Delhi 558, Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has held that there cannot be any deduction if domestic help is obtained from a family member.
This judgment was again relied upon by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case of Narayan Bahadur v. Sumeet Gupta and Anr., MAC APP. No. 762/11 dated 04.07.12.
